Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

maplore 0.0.0.9001

  • add_view_summary() gains:
    • style: "full" (the default), "compact" or "mini", a strip of three figures: the features in view, the statistic and the area of the view. compact = TRUE still works and means style = "compact".
    • show_area and area_unit: the area of the Earth covered by the screen, in km² or mi².
    • chart: the chart at the bottom of the panel. "histogram" (the default), "position" (a bar of all values with the view and the whole map marked on it), "strip" (one dot per feature), "split" (two histograms, the view above all features) or "none".
    • references: up to three other values to compare the view with, besides the whole map: fixed numbers, such as a target, or groups of features defined with the new reference_group(), such as a province. Their values are computed in R with the panel’s statistic and weight.
  • add_feature_search() gains collapsed: the search box starts folded into a button with a magnifying glass, which opens it, and folds back when it loses focus while empty. Useful on small maps, such as on phones.
  • add_view_summary() and add_view_ranking() gain fade = "moving": the panels fade while the map is panned or zoomed, so the map shows through, and come back when it stops.
  • New add_map_notes(): a small “Notes” button that opens a panel with context about the whole map: the source of the data, notes on what the figures do not include, and a link to learn more.
  • New add_rank_morph(): a button that lifts the polygons of a layer out of the map and lines them up, sorted by a column, all at the same size, with their rank, name and value; another click sends them back. Meant for up to 30 features; above 50 it gives an error.
  • New texts in context_labels(): area_zoom_in, ref_above, ref_below, ref_same, search_open, notes_title, notes_source, notes_link, morph_sort and morph_back.
  • maplore now imports jsonlite, which mapgl already uses, to read the layer’s data in R.

maplore 0.0.0.9000

  • First development version.
  • add_view_summary(): live summary of the features in view (count, mean, median or total, highest and lowest, histogram), compared with the whole map.
  • add_view_ranking(): the features in view with the highest or lowest values.
  • add_context_tooltip(): a tooltip with each feature’s rank, the share of features below it and its difference with the average.
  • add_feature_search(): a search box over a column of the map’s own data, ignoring case and accents.
  • context_labels(): texts for all the components, in English or Spanish.
  • Datasets: ar_departments, earthquakes and jp_prefectures.
